Project Location, Summary, and Budget Project Location: Lubbock State Supported Living Center 3401 N University Ave, Lubbock, TX, 79415 Project Summary: The Scope of Work includes, but is not limited to, the following: The Fire Alarm System Installing Contractor shall furnish all labor, equipment, and materials, and perform all operations in connection with the demolition of the existing fire alarm system and the installation of a new, addressable fire alarm system throughout the designated buildings on the Lubbock State Supported Living Center in Lubbock, Texas, as indicated and described in the contract drawings and specifications. Other than where noted by the design documents, the existing fire alarm system shall remain fully operational until acceptance of the new fire alarm system. Only compatible systems conforming exactly to the designated specifications, which include proposing only the brand name(s), make and model number(s) specified,will be considered. For complete Project information, refer to Attachment(s) H to Exhibit C, Project Specifications and Drawings (if there are separate drawings for the Project). Project Estimate: The approximate cost for construction of the Project is $3,676,427.00 Optional Pre-Proposal Webinar HHSC will conduct one (1) optional pre-proposal webinar that will be held on the date and time described below. Attendance at the pre-proposal webinar is optional. description: EMPLOYEES RETIREMENT SYSTEM OF TEXAS REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR TRANSMISSION TO INFORMATION RETURNS INTAKE SYSTEM (IRIS) SERVICES SOLICITATION NO. 26-15697-001 NIGP CODE: 208-00, 208-11, 208-36, 208-80, 920-17 The Employees Retirement System of Texas (ERS) has issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) seeking a qualified firm (Respondent) to provide an enterprise-grade tax compliance software to implement a transmission to Information Return Intake System (IRIS) for validating, processing, and electronically filing IRS Form 1099-R (Distributions from Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit-Sharing Plans, IRAs, Insurance Contracts, etc.). Respondent shall provide the level of services required in the RFP and meet other requirements that are in the best interests of ERS, its members, and the state of Texas (State). Respondent shall be required to execute a contract (Contract) satisfactory to, ERS for a period that begins upon execution of the Contract by ERS and extends for four (4) years, with an option to extend upon agreement of both parties. It is anticipated the Contract will be executed in October 2026. To be eligible for consideration, Respondent is required to submit its response to the RFP (Proposal) in accordance with the instructions set forth in the RFP. Respondents must meet the Minimum Requirements set forth in Section B of the Respondent Questionnaire (Appendix E). All Proposal materials shall be received by ERS via Euna Procurement no later than October 20, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. CT. The RFP is posted to the ESBD. To submit a Proposal, prospective Respondents must first create a profile in Euna Procurement (ERS’ e-procurement portal located at erstexas.bonfirehub.com),which operates best on the latest versions of Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome, and Mozilla Firefox. Browser cookies must be enabled when accessing Euna Procurement. Note that Respondent’s primary Proposal contact must create a Euna Procurement profile (with the actual contact person’s email address) and download the RFP documents in order to send and receive messages via Euna Procurement. ERS reserves the right to rebid the RFP if deemed by ERS to be in the best interests of ERS, its members, and/or the State. ERS also reserves the right to reject any Proposal submitted that does not fully comply with the RFP’s instructions and criteria. ERS is under no legal requirement to execute a Contract on the basis of this notice or upon issuance of the RFP and will not pay any costs incurred by any Respondent in connection with the preparation of a Proposal. ERS also reserves the right to revise any provisions set forth in the RFP at any time prior to execution of a Contract where ERS deems it to bein the best interests of ERS, its members, and/or the State. Any general questions should be sent to ERS’ point of contact, Office of Procurement and Contract Oversight, via Euna Procurement or ivendorquestions@ers.texas.gov. ERS’ mailing address is P.O. Box 13207, Austin, Texas 78711-3207.

General Scope of Work Project No. 1112666 titled “Centennial Program– New Park Development” is being solicited to develop a newly acquired over50,000 acre ranch tract in Edwards and Kinney Counties for a new Silver LakeState Park for the state of Texas. The tract’s geographiclocation is approximately Latitude 29°33’ N; Longitude 100°12’ W. The scope of this project includespre-construction services and construction of the new park development. The following list outlines the desired scopecomponents for the new park development. description: The Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center at El Paso (“TTUHSC EP”), a part of the Texas Tech University System, seeks proposals from qualified consulting firms to conduct a comprehensive needs assessment and develop a strategic plan for establishing a Diabetes Patient Navigation Program serving patients receiving medical care in El Paso, TX and the Borderplex region. The selected contractor will work collaboratively with TTUHSC El Paso leadership, Clinical Operations, clinical departments, institutional programs, patients, and community stakeholders to evaluate existing services, identify gaps in care coordination, and develop a comprehensive, sustainable, and scalable model for a centralized diabetes patient navigation program. The proposed program is intended to streamline the patient journey by improving coordination among medical providers, specialty clinics, pharmacies, diagnostic services, diabetes education programs, financial assistance and community resources. The planning process will identify opportunities to reduce barriers to care, improve patient access and continuity of care, reduce unnecessary duplication of services, and establish a framework for future program implementation. The initial program is anticipated to be piloted at the Texas Tech Physicians of El Paso's Alberta Avenue clinics. The contractor will assess the feasibility of this phased approach and develop recommendations to guide future implementation. This engagement is a planning and program-development project. The contractor will not be responsible for implementing or operating the navigation program unless separately authorized through a subsequent agreement.

description: The BRA is soliciting sealed proposals for the EWCRWS Infrastructure and Expansion The “1B1D PROJECT” represents two critical expansion improvements to the Brazos River Authority’s (BRA) East Williamson County’s Regional Water System Water Treatment Plant (EWCWTP); Phase 1B and Phase 1D. The Phase 1B Trinity Well Infrastructure Improvements will use cooling towers to treat up to 4 MGD of groundwater from the existing Trinity Well #1 for blending with treated surface water from Granger Lake. Trinity Well #1 is located on the campus of the EWCWTP. Additionally, Phase 1B work located at the EWCWTP includes significant chemical monitoring and distribution systems, stormwater system, upgrades to electrical and automation, and access road improvements that provide future buildout resilience. Phase 1B has schedule priority. The Phase 1D Short-term Expansion continues improvements at the EWCWTP to treat up to 13 MGD of additional surface water from Granger Lake by expanding raw water pumping capacity, upgrading storage reservoir inlets, outlets, and pumping capacity, upgrades to existing chemical systems, upgrades to electrical and automation systems, new rapid mix system, two new clarifiers, modify piping at four existing filters, four new additional filter systems, new backwash basin demolition of existing components and structures being replaced or removed, an additional 4.25 MG of finished water storage capacity for storage of blended treated groundwater (from Phase 1B) with treated surface water (from Phase 1D), and access road improvements. Phase 1D also includes a new medium service pump station for transmission of the finished water to the BRA’s existing and potential new customers, while providing future buildout resilience for longer term expansion.

description: LEGAL NOTICE Advertisement for Invitation for Bids October 13, 2026 Notice is hereby given that sealed bids will be accepted by the Jefferson County Purchasing Department for Invitation for Bid (IFB 26-066/MR) Garth Road Reconstruction Phase 1. Specifications for this project may be obtained from the Jefferson County website, https://jeffersoncountytx.gov/Purchasing/ or by calling 409-835-8593. Bids are to be sealed and addressed to the Purchasing Agent with the bid number and name marked on the outside of the envelope or box. Bidders shall forward an original and one (1) copy of their bid to the address shown below. Jefferson County does not accept bids submitted electronically. Late bids will be rejected as non-responsive. Bids will be publicly opened and read aloud in the Jefferson County Purchasing Department (1st Floor, Historic Courthouse) 1149 Pearl Street, Beaumont, Texas 77701, at the time and date below. Bidders are invited to attend the sealed bid opening. BID NAME: Garth Road Reconstruction Phase 1 BID NUMBER: IFB 26-066/MR DUE BY TIME/DATE: 11:00 AM CT, Wednesday, November 4, 2026 MAIL OR DELIVER TO: Jefferson County Purchasing Department 1149 Pearl Street, 1st Floor Beaumont, Texas 77701 There will be a Pre-Bid Conference and Walk-Through at 9:00 am CT on Thursday, October 22, 2026, at Jefferson County Engineering Department Conference Room located at 1149 Pearl Street, (Historic Courthouse 5th Floor), Beaumont, Texas 77701. The County shall require the Bidder to furnish a Bid Security in the amount of five percent (5%) of the total contract cost. The bid bond must be executed with a surety company authorized to do business in the State of Texas. Within ten (10) days after the date of contract execution and prior to the issuance of Notice to Proceed and/or Purchase Order, the Bidder shall furnish the following bonds: Performance Bond to the County for the full amount of the contract if the contract exceeds fifty-thousand dollars ($50,000). Payment Bond to the County for the full amount of the contract if the contract exceeds twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000.00). Any questions relating to these bid requirements should be directed to Mistey Reeves, Assistant Purchasing Agent at 409-835-8593 or via email at: mistey.reeves@jeffersoncountytx.gov. If no response in 72 hours, contact Deborah Clark, Purchasing Agent at 409-835-8593 or via email at deb.clark@jeffersoncountytx.gov. Jefferson County encourages Disadvantaged Business Enterprises (DBE/ACDBEs), Minority/Women Business Enterprises (M/WBEs), Small Business Concerns (HUBZone) and Veteran Heroes United In Business (VetHUB) to participate in the bidding process. Jefferson County does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age or disability in employment, or the provisions of services. Individuals requiring special accommodations are requested to contact our office at least seven (7) days prior to the bid due date at 409-835-8593. All interested firms are invited to submit a bid in accordance with the terms and conditions stated in this bid. Bidders are strongly encouraged to carefully read the entire invitation, as failure to return and/or complete all required documentation will result in a response being declared as non-responsive. Deborah L. Clark, Purchasing Agent Jefferson County, Texas

Grounds preparation will require manual removal of grass & weeds within the tree planting areas and individual 4 to 6 foot diameter rings around each tree planted. A variety of tree sizes from 3 gallon, 5 gallon, 7 gallon, 10 gallon, 15 gallon and balled & burlaped trees from 1.5 inch up to 4.5 inch caliper will need planting. Mulching of all trees will be required however all mulch, trees and any additional materials necessary for proper tree installation will be provided by Region One ESC. Contractor will be expected to provide their own shovels for digging and rakes for spreading mulch. Contractor is being asked to provide a an hourly rate per employee for regular hours and off hour/ holiday hour rates. Some projects will require a minimum 2 employees per day and a maximum of 3 to 4 employees per day. Contractor will not be responsible for any tree warranty however will be required to properly plant the trees according to Texas A&M Forest Service guidelines. Region One ESC is required to conduct a cost or price analysis for the procurement of goods and/or services not listed in the items tab, and within the scope of services offered with this bid solicitation. Location for Tree Plantings: Alton- Garcia Park and others Mission- La Lomita Park, Mission Hike & Bike Trails and others Edinburg- Vacker Park and others Donna- Hike & Bike Trails and other parks Mercedes- Mercedes Sports Complex & Walking Trails Harlingen- Bonham, Hunter, Rangerville and other parks San Benito- Resaca Trails, Stookey and other parks.
